- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- If model shows gradual upward trend with no spike, but true outcome spikes sharply, model underestimates volatility; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for 30d horizon if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- After a sharp price spike (true outcome > 75), model often overcorrects and flattens; apply upward bias correction for next 3–5 days if sentiment remains bullish.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 2–4% for 30d horizon.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model tends to underestimate price drop; apply downward bias correction by 1–5% for 30d horizon.
- If model forecast is flat or slightly rising while true outcome is volatile, model misses momentum; adjust forecast to match sentiment volatility (e.g., +1–3% if sentiment >0.5, -1–3% if sentiment <0.3).
- For 30d horizon, if sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often overestimates mean; apply mean reversion correction by subtracting 0.5–2% from forecast if recent 3–5 days show no trend.
- If model forecast is rising steadily and sentiment is bearish, model is lagging; apply downward correction by 1–3% for next 3–5 days if sentiment remains bearish.
- If model forecast is rising and true outcome is falling, model is overestimating bullish momentum; apply downward correction by 2–5% for 30d horizon if sentiment is bearish or neutral.
